title: Physical Design Intern
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job This team is responsible for defining and implementing the flow and methodology for the digital physical design of Lightmatter’s chips. We interface with multiple teams and utilize industry best practices to develop flows and methodologies which enable the physical design team to design and implement chips, while optimizing power, performance, and area. Responsibilities: Learn the Lightmatter physical design flow Improve the physical design flow through scripting in languages such as Python Investigate usage of AI to improve and augment the physical design flow Work with members of the physical design team on physical implementations or analysis Work with other teams in Lightmatter such as the analog design team or photonics team to collaborate on and improve mixed signal and mixed signal + photonics design methodologies Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Masters or PhD program Interest in physical design Familiar with TCL or Python scripting Knowledge of physical design tools and flows Understanding of the concepts of synthesis, place and route, and LVS/DRC Understanding of VLSI design fundamentals Willingness and curiosity to learn from an exciting team! Preferred Qualifications Research, lab, or prior internship experience in physical design involving photonics, semiconductors, or AI hardware Publications, projects, or open-source contributions related to physical design or python programming Prior experience or coursework relevant to physical design Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay determined based on the position and your location, year in school, degree, and experience. Hourly Rate in USD $50 $55 USD Benefits Comprehensive Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision) Retirement Savings Matching Program Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D) Generous Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays) Paid Family Leave Short Term & Long Term Disability Training & Development Commuter Benefits Flexible, hybrid workplace model Equity grants (applicable to full-time employees) Benefits eligibility may vary depending on your employment status and location. Lightmatter recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. Export Control Candidates should have capacity to comply with the federally mandated requirements of U.S. export control laws.

title: Analog Design Engineer Intern - GaN Device
description: We can't predict what the future holds, but we know Texas Instruments will have a part in shaping it. As a GaN/thin-film analog design intern you will bring focus on new GaN and thin film device design, testing and characterization. You will help benchmark and in-turn modify our device and process technology to make our customers’ visions a reality. You’ll design, characterize, model and enable productization of next generation of high voltage, RF and optoelectronic devices, with the opportunity to work in a lot of exciting areas and with industry experts. About the Position Kilby Labs is looking for a qualified internship candidate for the position of Analog Design Engineer with focus on GaN and TFT device technology: process- and device-design, characterization, modeling, and optimization of power, RF and optoelectronic applications. Background knowledge of device physics, compact model development, on-wafer test and measurement and data analysis is preferred. Master’s or Ph.D. (ongoing) candidates in Electrical and Computer Engineering with specialization in Integrated Devices, Circuits and Systems are preferred. Kilby represents an advanced research and product development support organization within TI chartered to define and develop new and innovative IP in collaboration with business units and customers. Kilby engineers must have the ability to approach new and/or existing problems from a different perspective in a way that results in unique, leap-frog technologies. In addition, Kilby engineers are required to take on all aspects of a project depending on project needs. Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: Design, optimize, and TCAD model power, RF and optoelectronic devices to understand device performance and bottlenecks arising from device construction Define and develop mixed optical and electrical test and characterization infrastructure Take on-wafer and in-package electrical tests: IVs, breakdown and CV tests Take optical test data: Impact of different wavelength (visible-UV) light illumination Analyze data and quantify generation efficiency, IQE, impact of BEOL metals on optical flux Study changes in electrical characteristics of device: VT/IDSAT/RDSON vs. optical flux or bias Define compact modeling requirements for such opto-electronic devices Work with circuit designers and system engineers to understand desired device figures-of-merit to guarantee competitive advantage in customer use-cases Come up with novel device architectures to address device and system requirements. Perform process flow simulations and recipe-optimization to realize those device-architectures, in collaboration with the process development teams Minimum Requirements: Ph.D. degree or currently working towards a Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering. Alternatively, masters degree with 3+ years of experience Strong background in GaN/thin film device physics, characterization, GaN compact modeling, optical testing and GaN/TFT processing Familiarity with GaN/TFT-process and device TCAD Experience in semiconductor technology development, modeling, test development, device/module qualification, Verilog-A coding, lab-management Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills Course work completed in: Physics of Semiconductor Devics, Process Technology and Device design, Integrated Circuit Design (Digital, Analog, Radio Frequency and Mixed Signal), Power Systems, Power Electronics, Compact modeling Preferred Qualifications: Ability to measure, quantify and come up with device solutions to improve optical performance of power devices Ability to test and characterize devices IV, CV, BV and study parametric response to optics On-wafer probe testing experience in both electrical and optical domains: Usage experience in handling B1500, SMUs, CMUs, probes Experience with device simulator tools like Sentaurus, Cadence, ADS, Verilog-A Ideal candidate must also excel at promoting new ideas, building collaborative relationships, working across organizations Strong verbal and written communication skills Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions Why TI? title: Research Scientist Intern - Materials Architecture & Device Integration
description: Meta’s Reality Labs Research is seeking innovative Research Scientist interns with a passion for technology to join our materials, manufacturing, and integration team at the research location in Redmond, WA. The ideal candidate will be a senior PhD student with a strong background in materials science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field; substantial hands-on experience in MEMS and microsystems integration; and a passion for turning new materials and processes into working devices. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year. Some projects may require a minimum of 16 consecutive weeks. About Reality Labs: Reality Labs is Meta’s research and development division dedicated to building the future of immersive technologies. Our mission is to advance the state of the art in virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and wearable devices to build systems that enhance human capabilities through intelligent machine collaboration and enable people to connect, collaborate, and experience the world in entirely new ways.

title: Hardware Test Engineer Intern
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job Are you ready to do meaningful internship work on technology that is changing how AI systems are built? The System Level Test team owns the final at-speed test of our silicon photonics products. These are cutting-edge high-speed optical interconnects built to move data between the processors that power AI datacenters, where copper is running out of reach and light is taking over. We build the test methods, the automation, and the data behind the pass vs fail decision. This summer's project is a hands-on optical characterization and correlation study aimed at improving how our products are tested in production. You will work on real optical hardware in the lab, build the measurement automation, generate the data, and write the recommendation that decides whether the approach moves forward. The result will directly influence how our next products are tested. Responsibilities: Characterize a set of silicon photonics units on bench optical instrumentation, measuring output power, modulation amplitude, extinction ratio, and wavelength. Build automation to run measurements, control the lab setup, and log results in a consistent, reusable data format. Correlate unit measurements against a calibrated laboratory reference and quantify per-unit offsets and population spread. Measure unit stability across time, temperature, and repeated re-insertion, and analyze repeatability and drift. Deliver a feasibility and gap assessment with a clear recommendation, including the calibration and maintenance scheme needed for production deployment. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering, or a related field. Coursework or project experience in at least one of: integrated circuit design, device or circuit characterization, or electrical or optical testing. Hands-on experience with standard lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, or optical power meters, from coursework, research, or a prior internship. Programming experience in Python or a similar language, including reading and plotting measurement data. Preferred Qualifications Research, lab, or prior internship experience in photonics or semiconductors. Experience automating lab instruments (PyVISA, SCPI, or similar). Familiarity with basic statistics: mean, standard deviation, repeatability, and gauge or measurement uncertainty. Publications, projects, or open-source contributions related to the role. Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay determined based on the position and your location, year in school, degree, and experience.
